### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4651070e85e92fd774e9d2b5cc458618943ef395` — the merge of head `c6a0810560dd2619f9785a43a588d3823a3041b3` into base `1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4651070e85e92fd774e9d2b5cc458618943ef395 && git checkout 4651070e85e92fd774e9d2b5cc458618943ef395
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e c6a0810560dd2619f9785a43a588d3823a3041b3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e && git merge --no-ff c6a0810560dd2619f9785a43a588d3823a3041b3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review: #31863 (E5, last part of #31677) at head 17781316. Verdict: CHANGES, one required fix. The fix goes in the shared reader, which E1 already shipped.**

**What passes.** The connector name goes through R's one resolver (`resolvePackageScopedName`, type `connector`) for the caller's package. Nothing else picks a holder. A refusal fails the node, names every candidate, and dispatches nothing. A connector registered in code is not a registry item, so it keeps ADR-0097 §4. The three narrowing cases are declared, the first-party count is 0, and the 8 pins plus 3 ablations are adequate. **Red lines 2 and 3 hold.**

**R1 (required): `flowCallerPackage` must read the body the engine runs. The fix lives in that one reader.**

Seat 3 asked about this directly, and the answer is **no**. On main, E1's `flowCallerPackage` (`engine.ts`, #31738) is `packagedFlowOwner(context.flowName)`. That is the loader's set keyed by bare name, so it answers P for *every* run of a flow named after one of P's flows. That includes runs whose armed body is an environment-authored override of P's flow: a package-less stored row, or a declared override in P's `.custom` pair.

ADR-0150 D3 settles this in the paragraph after (a)–(d): *"A reference written in an environment-authored overlay (ADR-0005) is the environment's reference. It resolves as a caller with no package … It never resolves from the package the overlay customizes."*

So on main today, E1's `subflow`/`map` name in such an override reads from P. With this PR, so does the override's `connectorId`. An administrator's override that names an environment-only instance is refused under D3 (a), and that narrowing appears in no changeset. #31850 (#31790, approval queues) has the same defect, and I sent it back with CHANGES at 07:20Z.

Root fix, made once, here:
- Record the armed contender's source for **every** registration of a flow, not only on a collision. The source is package, override or runtime. `armedFrom` on `getShadowedFlows()` is a boot receipt written only when two contenders met, and a runtime save of an override never writes it.
- `flowCallerPackage` answers the package only for a package arm, and `null` for an override or runtime arm.
- Do not infer the arm from the stamps: hydration grafts P's envelope onto a stored row, so `_packageId` on the body names P.
- Measure it on a real kernel, as #31754 taught. The boot pull's `resolveFlowContenders`/`classifyContender` and the protocol's `isServedOverrideRowOf` are where the fact already exists.
- Pins: P's flow overridden by a package-less row, whose connector_action names an environment-only instance, and whose subflow names an environment-only flow. Both must resolve with no package, as on main before E1. Run the pins with the fix ablated (red), then with it (green).
- Give the reader a public spelling that #31850's approval service can call with a flow name. The name is the seat's call. #31850 then reuses it instead of `packagedFlowOwner`. Land order: #31863 first.
- In the changeset, say that E1's subflow reader is corrected too. It is a loosening back to main's behaviour for overrides, so no new narrowing comes with it.

**Recorded for the connector backstop child (ADR-0150 D9).** Dispatch still goes through `resolveConnectorAction(cfg.connectorId)` by bare name. That is correct only while phase 1's one-holder refusal keeps the engine at one instance per name. The child that narrows the `connector` backstop owes dispatch to the **resolved holder's** instance, plus a pin for D+U where P→D.

Re-ping the epic seat with the new head.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #31863 at head 5e37bfd4: PASS.** Ready once CI is green and the dogfood and gates report is posted on this head.

**R1 is met at the root.**
- The engine records an arm at every registration (`flowArms`, keyed by the parsed body), and `armedFlowPackage(name)` answers the package only for a package arm.
- `flowCallerPackage` reads that answer. So the reader E1 shipped and E5's connectorId are corrected in the same change.
- I checked every non-test `registerFlow` caller on this head:
  - The plugin's four arming steps pass `entry.contender`: the boot pull, `resyncFlowsFromProtocol`, `syncFlowsFromProtocol` and the later step.
  - The runtime definition and clone doors (`registerAndSaveFlow`) pass no arm, so they land as `runtime` and are caller-less. That is right, because they are the environment's authoring doors.
  - `restoreFlowRegistration` puts the held body back, and that body keeps its arm by identity.
  - No other caller exists.
- The measured shape behind the fix is the useful finding: after `kernel:ready`, the served `.custom` override carries `_packageId` = base, and the old classifier answered `package` for it. Those 3 override shapes × connectorId/subflow are pinned, with package-arm CONTROLs and ablations that each turn red (6, 4 and 2 pins).
- The changeset records E1's correction as a loosening back to pre-E1 reading for overrides only. A package arm still narrows exactly as E1 declared. **Red lines 1–3 hold.**

**Recorded for later work:**
- #31850 (#31790) drops `packagedFlowOwner` and asks `armedFlowPackage(flowName)` for both the node slate and the decide-time tally. Its R1 is then met by reuse, so it lands after this PR.
- Card B #31696, which rekeys flows by (package, name), keeps the arm as the source of a run's package.
- The connector D9 backstop child owes dispatch to the resolved holder's instance (from my previous record).

#31677 closes when this merges. S3 #31684 then moves to `pm:queue`.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #31863 (Fixes #31677, ADR-0150 E5 last part) · 2026-11-09T09:01Z

Head-sha: `c6a08105`

- **Form:** draft to `main`. `Fixes #31677` is the last E5 PR, after connectors #31725, webhooks #31744 and email #31825. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, with three narrowing cases declared (outside the closure, sibling in the artifact included; D3 (a); two holders in the closure) and a first-party count of 0. `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **What lands:** `connector_action` resolves its `connectorId` through `resolvePackageScopedName` (type `connector`) for the calling flow's package. A refusal fails the node and names every candidate. A no-package caller, a code-registered connector, or a host without a resolver dispatches by name as before.
- **Epic R1, root fix (seat names 6735158321):** `registerFlow(name, definition, armedFrom?: FlowContender)` records the armed source at every flow registration, kept in a WeakMap keyed by the parsed body. `AutomationEngine.armedFlowPackage(name)` answers a package only for a package arm. `flowCallerPackage` reads it, so an environment override of P's flow (a package-less row, or a `.custom` override, including the served-envelope document at `kernel:ready`) reads with no package. This corrects E1's subflow reader too, which the changeset says. Overrides return to main's behaviour from before E1, so it is not a new narrowing. The classifier gap is fixed through `isServedOverrideRowOf`, with no new export.
- **Pins and ablations:** override × {`connectorId`, `subflow`} × {package-less row, `.custom` stored row, `.custom` served envelope}, each red with the fix ablated and green with it. CONTROL: a package arm still answers P. The real kernel is measured at the boot pull and after `kernel:ready`.

- **Gates:** `check-governed-merges --pr 31863`: NOT governed, 551 changed lines. K = 10 first-parent commits on `main` since the PR base, and a local merge with `main` is clean. CI on this head: 35 success, 15 skipped, 0 other. dispatch-gates: 73/73 exit 0, 0 not run. service-automation 3518 passed, typecheck and eslint clean. Full dogfood on `5e37bfd4`: 3662 passed, 0 failed.
- **Recorded for later (epic):** connector dispatch is still by bare name, which is safe only while phase 1's one-holder refusal stands. That belongs to the connector D9 backstop child, not this PR.
